name: WIEZEN
description: Wiezen (Belgian Whist) is a Belgian 4-player trick-taking game with bidding and temporary alliances. 52-card deck, 13 each. Last card dealt = trump. Contracts: Troel (3 Aces, 4th Ace holder = partner), Solo (alone), Abondance (9+ alone), Misère (no tricks), Open Misère, Pico (exactly 1 trick), Solo Slim (all 13).

content.text: Wiezen (Belgian Whist) is a Belgian 4-player trick-taking game with bidding and temporary alliances. 52-card deck, 13 each. Last card dealt = trump. Contracts: Troel (3 Aces, 4th Ace holder = partner), Solo (alone), Abondance (9+ alone), Misère (no tricks), Open Misère, Pico (exactly 1 trick), Solo Slim (all 13).

Wiezen is the Flemish word for Whist. It is a Belgian trick-taking game with bidding, descended from Boston Whist rather than the classic 19th-century Whist fashionable across Europe. It is related to British Solo Whist and Dutch Rikken. Documented in the Turnhout region (Leo Dignef's thesis on card games in the Turnhoutse) and from play in Ravels near Turnhout; it became the national card game of Flemish Belgium and remains deeply rooted in Belgian pub culture.
52 cards. A high. 13 each (4+4+5). Last card = trump.
13 each in packets. Cards NOT shuffled between hands (only cut).

items.text: Kleine Miserie optional: Many omit Kleine Miserie; Pico often included.
Troel before bidding: Some require Troel/Pass-Troel to be said before the bidding proper begins.
Ronde Pas (Totale Miserie): When everyone passes, a preset list of no-trump games is played in rotation (e.g. lose last trick, no Queens, fewest tricks).
Carte Blanche: Player with no J/Q/K may call Carte Blanche before bidding; only Miserie op Tafel and Solo Slim then allowed.
Vuilbakwiezen: Dealer gets 1 card; each opponent 17 then discards 4; dealer's card plus discards form dealer's hand.
